Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Bakary Yaou Sangaré, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Niger, on Monday afternoon to discuss and exchange views on Iran-Niger bilateral relations and international developments. The Iranian Foreign Minister thanked the people of Niger for expressing solidarity with the Iranian people in the face of the military aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime. The Iranian Foreign Minister also expressed satisfaction with the very good and growing relations between the two countries in all areas and appreciated Niger’s principled position against the instrumental use of the Board of Governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) against Iran. During the meeting, the two sides discussed ways to expand Iran-Niger bilateral relations as well as joint cooperation within the framework of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Emphasizing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to strengthen relations with African countries, particularly the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), the Foreign Minister expressed hope that a joint meeting between Iran and the three member states of the Alliance of Sahel States would be held as soon as possible. The Iranian Foreign Minister, recalling the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position in support of the independence and national sovereignty of developing countries, condemned the continued pressure and illegal interference by some Western countries, including France, in the internal affairs of African countries. He also underscored the Islamic Republic of Iran’s support for the efforts of the Nigerien government to safeguard the country’s independence and national sovereignty, maintain security and stability, and advance its development programs. The Iranian Foreign Minister also briefed his Nigerien counterpart on developments in the West Asia region and the Iranian people’s defense of their national sovereignty and territorial integrity in the face of military aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mali, on Monday afternoon. During the meeting, the two sides discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Mali bilateral relations and international developments. The Foreign Minister expressed appreciation for Mali’s principled positions in opposition to violations of the law and unilateral coercive measures, as well as for the solidarity expressed by the people and government of Mali with Iran in the face of the military aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime. Emphasizing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to strengthen relations with developing countries, including African countries, particularly the member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), the Foreign Minister announced Iran’s readiness to hold a joint meeting with the three member states of the Alliance of Sahel States. Recalling the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position in support of the independence and national sovereignty of all countries, Araghchi condemned the pressures and unlawful interference by certain European countries in the internal affairs of the Sahel countries, which have engaged in creating and financing terrorist groups and organized crime in the region. The Malian Foreign Minister expressed satisfaction with the growing trend in his country’s relations with Iran, outlined recent developments in Mali and the Sahel region, and stressed that his country and other African nations would not allow the colonial and interventionist ambitions of certain European governments to be realized.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations, on the final day of his trip. During the meeting, the Foreign Minister outlined the latest developments in the West Asia region following the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran, stressing that the Islamic Republic of Iran, as a founding member of the United Nations, has expected and continues to expect the Organization and its member states not to remain indifferent to the violation of law and gross breaches of the Charter by a permanent member of the Security Council, and to explicitly condemn the continuation of the United States’ unlawful interventionist measures and threats. Referring to the two rounds of unlawful US and Israeli attacks against Iran in the midst of negotiations within less than one year, as well as the continuation of acts of aggression in the form of a naval blockade and economic terrorism, the Foreign Minister stressed Iran’s determination to defend its national sovereignty and territorial integrity with all its capabilities. He stated that the Iranian nation will never abandon its demand for justice and for the prosecution and punishment of those who ordered and perpetrated the war crimes committed by the United States and the Israeli regime. Recalling Iran’s responsible approach toward international peace and security, Araghchi noted that the Islamic Republic of Iran has always remained steadfast in its commitment to using diplomacy as a means of safeguarding its national interests and ensuring peace in the region. However, he said, the United States has repeatedly betrayed diplomacy over the past decade and, by violating its commitments, has contributed to insecurity in the region. Araghchi also referred to the continuation of the Israeli regime’s genocide and warmongering in the occupied Palestinian territories, Lebanon, Syria and other countries in the region, and recalled the responsibility of the United Nations and the Security Council to end Israel’s impunity and halt the crimes being committed in Gaza and the West Bank. The UN Secretary-General, condemning violations of the fundamental principles of the Charter, particularly the use of force by superpowers, stressed the need for all countries to abide by the principles and rules of international law and to use diplomacy to resolve issues. The meeting also addressed the continued gross violations by the United States of the Host Country Agreement and its obstruction of the normal activities of Iran’s Mission. Iran’s protest over the performance of the host government in this regard was conveyed to the Secretary-General, who was urged to take the necessary measures to compel the US government to fulfill its obligations.

Zaid Raad Al Hussein, Chairman of The Elders, met and held talks with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Monday morning. Araghchi is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly. During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on international trends, existing challenges in international relations, threats to global peace and security, and ways to address these dangers and challenges. Referring to the main philosophy behind the establishment of the United Nations, namely respect for the national sovereignty of countries and preventing war and the use of force in relations among states, the Foreign Minister said restoring confidence in the Organization requires member states, particularly the permanent members of the Security Council, to adhere to the principles of the UN Charter. The Foreign Minister elaborated on developments over the past two years concerning Iran’s nuclear issue, describing the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran in the midst of negotiations as a flagrant violation of international peace and security. He stressed the responsibility of the United Nations and all countries to explicitly oppose flagrant violations of international law, as well as the crimes committed by the United States and Israel against Iran. The Foreign Minister stressed that the insecurity in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz has resulted from the unlawful and interventionist actions of the United States and the Israeli regime, and that the international community should hold them accountable for all the resulting humanitarian, security and economic consequences. The Chairman of The Elders, for his part, underscored the importance of the rule of law and all countries’ adherence, particularly that of major powers, to the UN Charter and international law. He condemned the unlawful use of force and aggression against countries and stressed the need for all countries to pay greater attention to the UN Charter.

The second anniversary of the martyrdom of the great Lebanese man and tireless mujahid of the Islamic world, Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, Secretary-General of Hezbollah of Lebanon, is an opportunity to honor a man who devoted his blessed life to advancing Islam, upholding the dignity and independence of Lebanon, defending the Palestinian cause, and confronting the occupation and expansionism of the Zionist enemy. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran honors the memory and path of Martyr Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, Martyr Sayyed Hashem Safieddine and other great figures and companions of the blessed tree of resistance, and pays tribute to the lofty soul of the martyred Leader of the Ummah, His Eminence Grand Ayatollah Martyr Sayyed Ali Khamenei. Honoring the memory of Martyr Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah and the other martyrs of the path of resistance, from General Qassem Soleimani and Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis to Ismail Haniyeh, Yahya Sinwar and Mohammad al-Ghamari, as well as the many honorable women and men and innocent children who have been martyred in the course of defending human dignity and honor against terrorism, occupation and colonial-Zionist-American domination, is an act of paying tribute to a school and an ideology that does not tolerate submission to oppression and is unwilling to sacrifice human dignity and honor in the face of occupation, apartheid and bullying. Over three decades of wise leadership of the Lebanese resistance against the aggression and occupation of the Zionists and their American supporters, the great Nasrallah established an unparalleled model of courage, insight, prudence and power in confronting the most sinister mafia gang in history, the impact of which will remain forever alive in the minds and culture of the people of Lebanon and the region. Undoubtedly, today the people of Lebanon and the region understand the value and significance of his struggle more than they did during his physical lifetime. Today, the people of Lebanon, the region and the world more than ever recognize this reality: confronting the occupation and warmongering of a racist and authoritarian regime that recognizes no limits in its crimes and brutality and honors no pledge or commitment requires the continuation of dignified resistance. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs once again strongly condemns the heinous and unforgivable crime committed by the Zionist terrorists in their attack on Lebanon and the assassination of Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah and his loyal companions, including Martyr General Abbas Nilforoushan, and reminds all countries of their moral and international legal duty to prosecute and punish the perpetrators and masterminds of this crime. Undoubtedly, neither the passage of time nor the repetition and accumulation of crimes will cause the slightest weakening of the demand for justice and the punishment of criminals. The Islamic Republic of Iran, recognizing Lebanon's critical position as a country situated in the vicinity of an occupying and terrorist entity, remains steadfast in its principled position of supporting Lebanon's independence, territorial integrity, sovereignty and national unity, and believes that a strong and independent Lebanon, capable of defending its people and territory, is one of the pillars of lasting stability and security in the entire region. وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ

In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا ۚ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ “And do not think of those who are killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” Two years have passed since the martyrdom of a Mujahid whose name is intertwined with the contemporary history of Lebanon and the West Asian region, as well as with decades of struggle to end occupation and defend the sovereignty, dignity and honor of the peoples of the region. Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, the martyred Secretary-General of Lebanon’s Hezbollah, was martyred in an attack by the criminal Zionist regime after years of prominent presence and a significant role in the political developments of the region. He belonged to a generation and lineage of men who learned politics amid occupation, war and the region’s successive crises, and who firmly believed that no nation can be deprived forever, through force, threats and intimidation, of its right to sovereignty, dignity and self-determination. For this reason, his name, beyond the framework of a political party or movement, has become permanently embedded in the contemporary memory of the region with concepts such as honor, steadfastness and resistance against occupation and the crimes of the Zionist regime. His martyrdom, although a profound loss for Hezbollah, the people of Lebanon and all free people around the world, once again demonstrated a historical reality: eliminating individuals never means eliminating the ideas and aspirations that are rooted in the historical experience of nations. The history of Lebanon, Palestine and the region has shown that deep-rooted political and historical issues cannot be eradicated through assassination, intimidation and elimination; for no nation can be made to abandon its demand for its rights and dignity by eliminating its heroes and leaders. Under the difficult circumstances following the loss of the “Sayyed of Resistance,” the assumption of the heavy responsibility of leading Hezbollah by Sheikh Naim Qassem, at a time fraught with difficulties and rapid developments, demonstrated the continuation of the path of seeking justice and resisting mounting pressures. Sheikh Naim Qassem’s leadership once again showed that firm belief in a cause can, even under the most difficult and complex circumstances, serve as a source of steadfastness, resolve and continuity along a path. Now, on the second anniversary of the martyrdom of Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, I honor his memory and name, as well as those of all the martyrs of the Resistance, and extend my condolences and congratulations on this occasion to the esteemed families of the martyrs, the honorable people of Lebanon, and all those who have stood in the path of freedom, independence and the dignity of their homeland.

item.title: UN humanitarian affairs chief meets Iranian Foreign Minister in New York
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs, on Saturday evening. During the meeting, regional and international developments, the humanitarian assistance situation in crisis-hit areas, and areas of cooperation between Iran and relevant UN bodies were reviewed. The Iranian foreign minister, referring to Iran’s long-standing hosting of Afghan refugees despite the US economic war and unjust sanctions, highlighted the responsibility of international humanitarian organizations in this regard. Araghchi also referred to the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the West Bank resulting from the genocide and crimes committed by the Israeli regime, as well as the displacement of hundreds of thousands of people in Lebanon due to Israel’s ongoing attacks, stressing the need for greater attention by the United Nations and international humanitarian organizations to these situations. Araghchi recalled that addressing humanitarian crises and disasters in a fundamental manner requires tackling the causes and factors that give rise to them. The UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs, for his part, outlined the most important humanitarian situations around the world and stressed the continuation of UN efforts to fulfill its humanitarian responsibilities.

In all these meetings, our main focus was to state the conditions of the Islamic Republic of Iran for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and for the advancement of the negotiations—conditions that have been set by the Supreme National Security Council. 🔹 We were tasked with explaining and presenting these conditions here and defending them. Thankfully, this was formally done in all the meetings we held. In the meetings we had with the mediators, these conditions were fully conveyed, explained and elaborated upon, and they also conveyed these matters to the American side. 🔹 We defended our positions, our policy and the conditions we had set in all the meetings, and the entire world, particularly fair-minded countries around the world, became aware that the Islamic Republic of Iran, just as it has defended its country well, has consistently demonstrated strength in the diplomatic arena as well, and in particular, by presenting various proposals and establishing a diplomatic path, has been able to steer the diplomatic environment in its own favor. 🔹 The proposals we put forward were discussed in interviews, explained and also raised in the meetings. They were also conveyed to the American side through intermediaries. 🔹 We saw the first reaction from the US president, but nothing has yet been conveyed to us by the mediators. Of course, the US president has also made many positive statements as well as many contradictory ones, which, unfortunately, we hear from him quite often. We are waiting for the definitive views to be conveyed to us through the intermediaries, and we will make a decision based on them. 🔹 In any case, our conditions are clear, and any move forward toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon these conditions being met, and we will not back down from them. 🔹 The outlook for the Iranian people is a bright one. The Iranian people have demonstrated their strength in the military arena, the diplomatic arena, and also in the economic arena and in confronting sanctions. 🔹 Our enemies have also tried every possible path; they pursued every avenue they could and failed to achieve results. There will be no way forward other than a negotiated solution based on dignity and justice, while securing the rights of the Iranian people and meeting their legitimate demands. 🔹 Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this impasse. This is our position. Many countries share this position with us and understand it. 🔹 There is no one in the world today who can accuse the Islamic Republic of Iran of not having tried the path of diplomacy. In this respect, we are in a stronger political position, because we have never closed the path of diplomacy or negotiations, while at the same time we have never backed down from our rights. 🔹 Whenever our enemies chose another path, we also stood firmly against them on that path.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Mohamad Hasan, Foreign Minister of Malaysia, on Saturday morning. The Foreign Minister appreciated Malaysia’s principled positions in condemning the military aggression against Iran and the war crimes committed, stressing Iran’s determination to defend its security and national sovereignty against the aggressive and interventionist actions of the United States. The Iranian Foreign Minister outlined developments related to the US-Israeli imposed war against Iran, the United States’ breach of its commitments, and its economic terrorism against the Iranian people, stressing that developing countries should work to safeguard their common interests and counter the United States’ lawlessness and destructive unilateralism. The Iranian Foreign Minister also briefed his Malaysian counterpart on the latest developments concerning the Strait of Hormuz, including the status of the bilateral Iran-Oman understanding on establishing safe shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, stressing that the sole factor behind the continued insecurity in the waterway is the aggressive actions of the United States. The two sides discussed the need for greater cooperation and coordination among Islamic countries, including within the framework of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, to counter the genocide and crimes committed by the Zionist regime in the occupied Palestinian territories and other countries of the region. The two sides also stressed the continuation of consultations and the expansion of bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest.
